source_text: Maximam autem dico, non quia diabolum magis reum fuisse diffitear, sed quia, cum institutionis ratio peteretur, accommodatius Apostolus hominis, quem plurimum successio humanitatis aspexit, quam aeriae substantiae fecerit mentionem. Verum in ipsa humanitate primam mulierem deliquisse constabat; sed quia patrum in omnibus efficacior est et maior auctoritas, eum dixit formam fuisse peccati, non a quo coepit delictum, sed qui per potestatem sexus virilis magis fuisse probatur imitabilis. Vides nempe, ut consequentia intellectus veritatem sibi inesse testetur.
pass_a_gloss: But I say the greatest, not because I would deny that the devil was more a defendant, but because, when a reason of institution was being sought, the Apostle more fittingly made mention of a human being, whom the succession of humanity looked at most, than of an airy substance. But in humanity itself it stood that the first woman had offended; but because the authority of fathers is in all things more effective and greater, he said that he had been a form of sin, not from whom the offense began, but who through the power of the male sex is more proved to have been imitable. You see namely how the consequence of understanding testifies that truth is in itself.

lemmas.lexica: LS imitatio; Blaise moral copying vs generation of sin
LS delictum; Blaise Rom 5 delictum vs donum
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: I say ‘greatest’ not because I deny that the devil was more guilty, but because, when a basis for instruction was being sought, it was more fitting for the apostle to mention a human being, to whom successive generations of humanity especially looked, than a being of airy substance. Within humanity itself, however, it was established that the first woman sinned first (Genesis 3:6; compare 1 Timothy 2:14). But because fathers’ authority is more effective and greater in all things, he called the man the model of sin—not the one with whom the offense began, but the one who, through the power of the male sex, is shown to have been more readily imitated. You see how the coherence of the interpretation testifies that truth is within it (Genesis 3:6) (1 Timothy 2:14).

choices.why: Julian's Rom 5:12 reading: sin passes by copying Adam's example, not by generation/seed.
Paul's delictum of the one man; an act, not a nature.
